headline: Mississippi elected a Black senator. First since 1881.
summary: Democrat Scott Colom beat Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith in Mississippi by fewer than 5,000 votes out of nearly a million. He is the first Black senator from the state in more than 140 years, and the first Democrat it has sent since 1982. Hyde-Smith conceded Wednesday in a video. Democrats will hold 55 Senate seats, with Alaska still to be called.
cover_answer: Fewer than 5,000 votes out of nearly a million.
table_question: Lose by a whisker: shake hands, or demand a recount?

5-7.script: Mississippi has a new senator, Scott Colom. Nearly a million people voted, and he won by fewer than 5,000. If 200 kids voted on a game, that is winning by one kid. He is the first Black senator from Mississippi in more than 140 years. The grown-ups have it.
5-7.why: One kid in 200 is a margin a six-year-old can picture. The history gets one sentence.
5-7.why_long: A six-year-old reasons from what is in front of them, so the script turns a million votes into 200 kids and a win by one. The 140 years gets one plain sentence; a child this age cannot yet hold what it means, and does not need to. Expect 'did the other lady cry?' She said she respects what the voters decided and wished him well. Say so.

8-12.script: Scott Colom drove to all 82 Mississippi counties and ran on prices, calling his opponent "Cindy High Prices" over Trump's tariffs. He won by fewer than 5,000 votes, the first Democrat there since 1982. That close, you'd want the ref to check the replay. Mississippi has no recount law, so she conceded.
8-12.why: A chain they can follow: prices, 82 counties, 5,000 votes, no replay rule.
8-12.why_long: At ten they are working out rules, so the script hands over a chain: prices, 82 counties, a win by 5,000, and a state with no recount rule. The replay is the mechanism they know from every close game. Expect 'is it fair to win by that little?' Yes. One more vote wins, and both sides knew the rule going in.

13-17.script: Trump won Mississippi by 22 points. Two years on, it sent a Democrat to the Senate by fewer than 5,000 votes. What flipped it: prices, or a candidate who went to all 82 counties against one who rarely showed up? Second: no recount law, so she conceded fast. Strength, or no option?
13-17.why: Two true things: a Trump state, and the Democrat it chose.
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold two true things: Mississippi went for Trump by 22 points and then elected a Democrat. The script asks what moved it, prices or a candidate who turned up, and whether a concession with no recount law behind it is grace or arithmetic. Expect 'did Black voters decide it?' The NAACP chairman says the organising did.

5-7.a: Helps make the country's rules in Washington. Every state sends two. Mississippi just picked one of its two.

8-12.a: No recount law in Mississippi. A court would have to order one.

8-12.q: Why is this a big deal?
8-12.a: No Democrat had won there since 1982. Trump won the state by 22 points.

13-17.a: Under 5,000 votes of nearly a million. 49.2% to 48.7%.
Not by law. A court would have to order one. She conceded.
